android.desc:
Tripot is a personal finance and budgeting app that helps you take control of your money with a simple, visual, and effective experience. Track income and expenses, manage budgets, plan recurring payments, and get a complete view of your financial life in one place.

Whether you want to monitor daily spending, stay on top of your income, save for a goal, or manage your finances while traveling, Tripot helps you build better money habits and make smarter financial decisions every day.

Designed to simplify personal finance management, Tripot acts as your financial companion. Create wallets with custom currencies and budgets, record transactions in seconds, and stay informed with clear insights into your financial situation—all through a modern, intuitive, and customizable interface.

Tripot makes it easy to organize your finances without spreadsheets or complexity. Categorize transactions, schedule recurring income and expenses, track upcoming payments, and visualize your cash flow. If you share expenses with friends, family, your partner, or travel companions, Tripot helps you split costs and keep balances organized.

**Key Features**

• Track income and expenses in one place
• Custom budgets and spending limits
• Multiple wallets with custom currencies
• Shared expenses and balance tracking
• Recurring income, bills, and scheduled transactions
• Categories and tags for detailed analysis
• Cash flow and financial overview dashboards
• Modern, intuitive interface with dark mode support

Tripot is more than an expense tracker—it's your personal finance hub. Manage your money, stay organized, and confidently plan for your financial future.

Note: Tripot does not provide banking, lending, investment, or financial services. It is designed to help you organize and manage your personal finances.

quotes.text:
I built a personal finance app after struggling with apps that were too complex or required constant internet.

This one is offline-first, syncs only when needed, and focuses on entering expenses as fast as possible.

It’s built with Angular + Capacitor, using IndexedDB for local storage. One challenge was keeping the UI responsive while handling large transaction lists and background sync.

I also tried to simplify the UX by reducing the number of steps to log an expense as much as possible.

One thing that hasn’t worked well yet is retention — many users try it once but don’t come back. I’m currently experimenting with onboarding and ways to make the app more engaging.

Would love feedback, especially on onboarding, UX, and retention.

Android app: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=ec.factor.expenses
